item.title: A Map of Distributed Consensus: From Paxos to DAG-BFT — Boundaries and Selection Across Four Families
item.description: etcd uses Raft, Cosmos uses Tendermint, Bitcoin uses PoW, Sui uses Mysticeti — they’re all “consensus,” but they do not solve the same problem. Electing a leader among a few known nodes in a datacenter and reaching agreement on a ledger among anonymous nodes on a public chain sit a full order of magnitude apart in their assumptions. Mashing every consensus algorithm onto one throughput axis is why so many selection guides read like mush.

item.title: The Ghost of Byzantium: From the Generals' Dilemma to Blockchain Consensus
item.description: Byzantine fault tolerance (BFT) is one of the most-cited ideas in distributed systems, yet few can explain where the name comes from. It wasn’t a theorem invented one morning — it grew, step by step, out of an aviation fault-tolerance project, a paper nobody read, and a name chosen because it would travel. This essay follows that thread chronologically, from a 1978 flight-control computer to the voting layer of every modern blockchain.
